campaign: 2026-10-05: the first energy-per-token measurement. Pi 5, TinyLlama-1.1B Q4_K_M, prefill-only and decode-only phases at the wall (testbed/energy.md 'First run at home' 3)

model.verified: sha256sum on the Pi 5 at 14:48, matching testbed/models.md; the runner re-checks it in preflight and refuses on a mismatch

build: llama.cpp b23701f7 (clean tree), build 200, ~/llama.cpp/build/bin/llama-bench on the Pi 5

plan.order: settle 30 s; idle 300 s; then pp1, tg1, pp2, tg2, pp3, tg3 (10 s gaps); idle 300 s
plan.pp: llama-bench -m <model> -t 4 -p 512 -n 0 -r 20 --progress -oe jsonl (about 126 s timed per invocation at the 81.26 t/s characterisation)
plan.strip: shelly_strip.py log at 5 Hz for the whole session; outlet 1 = pi5, confirmed by load 2026-10-05
plan.board_sampler: get_throttled, temperature, ARM clock, fan state, load average every 5 s for the whole session

definitions.window: from the laptop stamp of the first timed repetition's progress line to the stamp of the first result line after the last repetition (shakedown 14:56: result line 0.749 s after the last repetition started, the line arriving promptly through ssh with stdbuf -oL); model load and warm-up outside
definitions.tokens: n_prompt x reps (pp) or n_gen x reps (tg), from llama-bench's jsonl
definitions.net_energy: gross energy over the window minus the idle-before mean power x window length, by each method (shelly_strip.py summarise --idle)
definitions.j_per_token: net energy / tokens; Wh per 1,000 tokens = J/token x 1000 / 3600
definitions.methods: both reported: the strip's counter and the trapezoid of apower. Which to quote is NOT decided here (open: the QR6 reference); every figure is 'as measured by the strip at the wall', adapter included
definitions.spread: across the three invocations of a phase: 100 x (max - min) / mean (the house rule's across-run spread)

basis.tps: characterisation 2026-09-27 19:18 (b23701f, -r 3, start 35 C): pp512 81.26 t/s, tg128 18.13 t/s on the Pi 5 at 4 threads; band +/- 5 %
basis.mean_w: outlet 1 read 7.39 W under a 4-core busy loop and 2.31 W idle (2026-10-05). Prefill is SIMD-heavy (guessed above the busy loop), decode memory-bound (guessed below or near it). These bands were chosen before the 14:56 shakedown and are unchanged, but the shakedown's 2-3 s windows (flagged TOO_FEW_SAMPLES) showed about 9.1 W prefill and 8.2 W decode, so the power bands are NOT fully blind
basis.j_per_token_net: from the power bands and the t/s points, minus the 2026-10-05 idle floor range on outlet 1 (2.31 W apower to 2.45 W counter)
basis.spread: the house rule: the same config minutes apart drifts ~2 %
basis.gap: outlet 1 at idle 2026-10-05: -5.58 %; the router at 8.8 W: -5.49 %; if the gap is proportional it should hold under load

scoring: testbed/scripts/score_energy_phase_run.py: each check PASS / FAIL / N/A (a missing value never passes). Reported as found, whatever the outcome
conditions: Pi 5 booted ~13:46 by the strip's power-up, desktop session running, fan (pwm-fan) automatic; Pi 4 and Jetson idle on outlets 0 and 2 (the Jetson's guard running); the strip on 'WIFI-B' (fw 2.0.1, SNTP change pending a restart); the strip's web UI open in the Claude browser pane
